skill.name: building-chat-interfaces
skill.description: Build ChatKit interfaces with React, Python backends, authentication, persistence, page context, and Next.js cookie proxies.
skill.summary: Connect ChatKit frontends to authenticated custom backends with persistent conversations and contextual prompts.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: All 52 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, expected network calls, and normal environment configuration. Semantic review found three high-severity design risks involving untrusted prompt content, access tokens in model instructions, and client-controlled identity forwarding.

remediation.issue: Conversation history is inserted into agent instructions without a trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Keep user messages in user-role input, delimit contextual data, and apply prompt-injection controls before enabling tools.

remediation.issue: Access tokens are placed in model instructions and sent to any MCP tool.
remediation.suggestion: Keep tokens in server-side credential storage and attach them only inside an allowlisted tool transport after authorization.

remediation.issue: The proxy forwards X-User-ID from a client-controlled request header.
remediation.suggestion: Derive the user identifier from the verified token server-side and discard any client-supplied identity header.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Conversation History Becomes Agent Instructions
semantic_findings.description: Previous message content is concatenated into the Agent instructions string without role separation or delimiting. A malicious message can inject instructions and influence tool behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample directly joins stored message content and places it in the privileged instructions field. No trust boundary or prompt-injection defense is shown.

semantic_findings.title: Access Token Exposed to Model and MCP Tools
semantic_findings.description: The guidance inserts an access token into model instructions and says to include it when calling any MCP tool. This can disclose credentials to untrusted tools.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample explicitly formats access_token into SYSTEM_PROMPT and directs the agent to pass it to ANY MCP tool. The exposure is direct and unambiguous.

semantic_findings.title: Client-Controlled User Identity Forwarded by Proxy
semantic_findings.description: The authenticated proxy forwards X-User-ID directly from the incoming request. A caller can spoof another user if the backend relies on this header.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The proxy reads an authentication cookie but copies X-User-ID from request.headers instead of deriving identity from the verified token.

content.user_title: Build ChatKit Interfaces with Custom Backends
content.value_statement: Production chat interfaces need authentication, persistence, context, and reliable backend integration. This skill provides focused React, Python, and Next.js implementation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows a Python ChatKitServer subclass that runs a custom agent and streams responses.
Configures React useChatKit with custom request handling, authentication checks, and contextual metadata.
Demonstrates asynchronous database setup and connection pool warmup.
Provides JWT, JWKS, and Next.js httpOnly cookie proxy patterns.
Extracts page details and selected text for contextual chat requests.
Handles ChatKit web component loading before rendering the interface.
limitations: The examples are reference snippets, not a complete runnable application.
The verification script checks file presence only.
Streaming lifecycle events and interactive widgets belong to related skills.
Authentication examples require security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Add ChatKit to a React product
use_cases.description: Connect a React chat interface to a custom backend while sending page context and authenticated requests.

use_cases.title: Build a persistent chat backend
use_cases.description: Extend ChatKitServer, stream agent responses, and configure asynchronous database persistence.

use_cases.title: Proxy cookie-based authentication
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js route that reads httpOnly cookies and streams backend responses to the browser.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a ChatKit interface for [application]. Use React for the frontend and [backend framework] for the API. List required components and request flow.

prompt_templates.title: Add authenticated requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my useChatKit setup for [authentication provider]. Require login and send requests through [backend URL]. Keep credentials outside browser-readable storage.

prompt_templates.title: Create a cookie proxy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Next.js ChatKit proxy for an httpOnly cookie named [cookie name]. Derive identity from the verified token and preserve SSE streaming.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ChatKit architecture for tenant isolation, prompt injection, token handling, persistence, and streaming. Identify risks and propose concrete code changes.

output_examples.input: Plan a React and Python ChatKit integration with authenticated users.
output: React uses useChatKit with a custom request handler.
The backend verifies authentication before creating request context.
ChatKitServer streams the custom agent response.
Persistent storage scopes threads to the verified user.

output_examples.input: Explain how to support an httpOnly authentication cookie.
output_examples.output: A same-origin Next.js route reads the cookie server-side, verifies it, derives the user identity, forwards the request, and preserves SSE headers.

output_examples.input: Add page context to chat requests.
output_examples.output: Collect a limited set of page fields, send them as untrusted metadata, validate them on the backend, and delimit them from agent instructions.

best_practices: Derive tenant identity from a verified token on the server.
Treat conversation history and page context as untrusted model input.
Preserve streaming response bodies and required SSE headers through proxies.
anti_patterns: Do not place access tokens in prompts or model-visible metadata.
Do not trust client-supplied user identifiers for data isolation.
Do not expose private environment variables through browser configuration.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React with useChatKit, Python with ChatKitServer, and Next.js route proxies.

faq.question: Does it provide a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns that require adaptation, integration, and testing.

faq.question: Can it support httpOnly authentication cookies?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates a server-side Next.js proxy that reads cookies and forwards streaming requests.

faq.question: Does it include conversation persistence?
faq.answer: It shows asynchronous database configuration and loading prior thread items for agent context.

faq.question: Does it cover interactive ChatKit widgets?
faq.answer: No. Widget actions, templates, and composer tools are assigned to a related skill.

faq.question: Are the authentication examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Production use requires server-derived identity, restricted token handling, authorization checks, and prompt-injection defenses.
